name: Dog walking and pet sitting

not_yet: Don't skip the meet and greet.
Don't take dogs you can't handle in your first month.
Don't pay for a booking app before you have 3 regulars.
crowd.note: Trust first. Summer and the holidays are the busiest weeks for sitting.
crowd.basis: Scores, buyer, first $1 and not-yet lines: research/crowd.json (our judgment). Best months: research/niches/petcare.json crowd hint (walking is steady all year; sitting peaks in summer and the holidays).

safety: Every new client starts with a free meet and greet at their home.
Get the intake form filled in before the first visit: vet, emergency contact, meds, food and behavior notes.
Don't take dogs you can't handle in your first month.
Never label keys with a client's address.
Platform protection plans don't cover clients you book directly: get your own liability and pet care insurance before you hold keys.
Boarding pets in your own home can need a state license, plus zoning, lease or HOA okay. Start with walks and drop-ins.

extra.title: Meet and greet script (20 minutes, free)
lines: 1. Thanks for having me. I'll let your pet come to me first.
2. Walk me through a normal day: food, walks, potty breaks, anything they're scared of.
3. Any health issues, meds or allergies? Who is your vet, and who should I call if I can't reach you?
4. Leash, harness, doors and gates: what are your rules? Any dogs or people they don't get along with?
5. Keys or door code: how do you want to hand them over? I never label keys with your address.
6. Let's do a short walk together so you can see how we do.
7. My founding price is {founding}. Want to set up the first week?

offer.name: 30-minute dog walk

includes: A free meet and greet at your home before the first walk
A 30-minute walk on a route you approve
Fresh water and a paw wipe when we get back
A visit card after every walk: times, potty, notes and a photo
steps: Free meet and greet: your pet meets me, you show me the routine.
You fill in a short intake form: vet, emergency contact, food, meds and rules.
Walks happen at the time you book, with your rules followed.
After every visit you get a visit card with a photo.
offer.promise: If I'm late or miss a walk, the next one is free. If you're not happy with a visit, tell me the same day and I refund that visit.
offer.promise_note: I can't promise how your pet will behave. I promise the care: every walk as booked, your rules followed, and a card after every visit.

partner_objections.label: They have rules
partner_objections.means: They have rules about posting or promoting.
partner_objections.answer: Thanks for explaining, and of course I'll follow your rules. Is there another way you share local services with clients or residents, like a newsletter or a resource list, that I could apply for?
partner_objections.next: Follow their rules exactly and ask about the approved way in.

objections.label: Why not Rover or Wag?
objections.means: They're comparing you with the booking apps.
objections.answer: Fair question, and the apps work for lots of people. With me you get the same walker every time, no booking fee on top of the walk, and a free meet and greet first. One thing worth knowing: Rover's own protection doesn't cover bookings made outside Rover, so ask to see my insurance certificate.
objections.next: Mention the meet and greet, then book it.
objections.check: Have your insurance certificate ready before you send this.

sources.says: Owners pay an 11% booking fee on Rover.
Wag adds a $2.99 booking fee per walk, waived with Wag Premium.
Rover's protection excludes bookings made outside Rover.com.

objections.label: Are you insured?
objections.means: They want to know you carry insurance.
objections.answer: Good question to ask. I'll send you my insurance certificate before the meet and greet, so you can see exactly what it covers.
objections.next: Send the certificate, then book the meet and greet.
objections.check: Only send this once your policy is active.

sources.says: Ask for references and find out if the pet sitter is licensed and insured.
Clients almost always expect liability insurance and bonding.

objections.label: Can I trust you with my keys?
objections.match: \b(keys?|lockbox|door code|garage code|trust (you|a stranger|someone)|my home|our home|in my house)\b
objections.means: They want to know their home is safe with you.
objections.answer: Of course, it's a fair thing to ask. We meet first at your home, I'm happy to share my background check, keys are never labeled with your address, and they come back to you or go in a lockbox, whichever you prefer.
objections.next: Offer the meet and greet so they can see how you work.
objections.check: Have your background check ready to share before you send this.

sources.says: Clients verify a background check before handing over keys.

objections.label: My dog needs extra care
objections.means: Their pet needs extra care, and they want to know you can handle it.
objections.answer: Thanks for telling me. For a dog like that I walk solo, never in a group, we do a longer meet and greet so they get used to me, and we write the care plan down together. Any extra care is priced up front.
objections.next: Book a longer meet and greet. Only say yes if it's a dog you can handle.

sources.says: Walkers can walk a dog alone or with a vetted pack; be clear about your dog's personality and needs.

objections.label: Too much every weekday
objections.means: The price adds up for them over a week.
objections.answer: That's fair. Two ways to make it work: a 15-minute potty break instead of a full walk, or a pack of 5 walks paid ahead for a little less per walk.
objections.next: Hold your price. Offer the potty break or the pack of 5.

sources.says: Package discounts 5% to 10% for weekly commitments.

objections.label: What if you get sick?
objections.match: \b(if you('re| are) sick|you get sick|your (vacation|holidays?)|backup|back-up|cover for you)\b
objections.means: They want to know what happens when you can't come.
objections.answer: Good question. If I'm ever sick, I'll tell you as early as I can and only send a backup you've met and okayed. My holiday dates go out a month ahead.
objections.next: Put your backup and holiday policy in your agreement.
objections.check: Name your backup sitter before you promise one.

Meet and greet: Let the pet come to you and watch how they react.
Tour the home: leash, harness, food, treats, towels and bags.
Get the intake form filled in: vet, emergency contact, food, meds and behavior notes.
Agree on keys or the door code. Never label keys with the address.
Sign the service agreement with your cancellation and holiday terms.
Every visit: Check in, then potty and walk. Log the route and the time.
Fresh water, food and meds exactly as written.
Clean up any mess and lock up behind you.
After: Send the visit card with a photo.
Return or store keys as agreed.

sources.says: Arrange a meet and greet: watch the pet's body language, tour the home, go over where essentials are.
Use a standardized intake process to gather veterinary records, feeding instructions and emergency contacts.
